newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary sees forint devaluation of 11pc in 1998.
newsitem.headline: Hungary sees forint devaluation of 11pc in 1998.

text.p: The three-year forecast of the Hungarian government includes 11 percent average annual forint devaluation for 1998, nine percent for 1999 and 7.5 percent for the year 2000, the Finance Ministry said on Wednesday.
The Finance Ministry published on Wednesday the detailed government forecasts for the next three years approved by the government last week together with its anti-inflation programme.

National Bank of Hungary Deputy President Gyorgy Szapary stressed at a news conference that the devaluation rates included in the government document are forecasts and the government and central bank will decide on the actual devaluation rates later.
He said the decisions would be made based upon inflation and economic competitiveness figures.
"Inflation and competitiveness are equal priorities," he told Reuters.
Hungary currently has a crawling peg forint devaluation system with a monthly depreciation rate of 1.1 percent.
Szapary did not make it clear for how long Hungary wanted to maintain the crawling peg devaluation system.
